lucrezia_italian.txt: Ciao a tutti e bentornati sul mio canale, oppure benvenuti se questo è il primo video che guardate qui sul mio canale.

summary.text: Three things to carry from last time.
I wake up — the reflexive pronoun goes in front.
it takes time — it agrees with the thing needed.
quality of life — vita has no written accent.
the toothbrush. Before s plus a consonant the masculine article is lo, not il.
I don't remember the name. But before a verb you need di —
And four, two verbs English keeps as one.
I know this place. Places and people take conoscere; facts take sapere.

shortened.text: Start with what carries over.
mi sveglio
the reflexive pronoun in front of the verb. Today that pattern does most of the work.
First, an article rule that decides how a lot of words sound.
Before s plus a consonant, the masculine article is lo.
lo spazzolino
the toothbrush.
lo specchio
the mirror.
lo stadio
the stadium.
The test is s plus a consonant, not the letter s on its own — so it also catches
lo psicologo
the psychologist, and
lo zucchero
the sugar. Even borrowed words obey it:
lo standard
the standard. In the plural they all take gli —
gli stadi
the stadiums.
Second, reflexive verbs, carrying straight on from last time.
Mi siedo alla scrivania.
I sit at the desk — and there is alla again, a plus la.
Mi preparo per la lezione di italiano.
I get ready for the Italian lesson.
Lei si alza alle otto.
She gets up at eight.
Ti tagli i capelli?
Are you getting your hair cut? It is reflexive because the hair is yours — Italian marks that and English does not.
Noi ci sediamo al bar e beviamo un caffè.
We sit at the bar and drink a coffee.
Some reflexives are reciprocal — the -si means one another, not oneself.
incontrarsi
to meet each other.
Ci incontriamo in centro a Napoli.
We meet in the centre of Naples.
occuparsi
to deal with, to look after — and it takes di.
Lei si occupa di appartamenti per i militari.
She handles apartments for the military.
Third, remembering, which splits in two.
Non ricordo il nome.
I don't remember the name — a direct object, no pronoun.
Non mi ricordo.
I don't remember — reflexive, standing alone. Both are correct.
But in front of a verb it needs di.
Non ricordo di prendere le medicine.
I don't remember to take the medicine.
Non ricordo niente.
I don't remember anything — and that double negative is required, not optional.
And two phrases worth having ready in every lesson.
Non capisco.
I don't understand.
Non ti seguo.
I'm not following you — softer, because you're following the person rather than the words.
Finally, the pair English collapses into one word.
Conosco questo posto.
I know this place. Conoscere is for places and people you are acquainted with.
So parlare italiano.
I know how to speak Italian. Sapere is for facts and abilities. Use sapere for a place and it will sound wrong.

errori.text: From the recording — three things worth fixing.
For a place, use conoscere, not sapere.
a plus la is never two words.
And locazione is a false friend — it means a lease, not a location.

sec-lo.text: One article rule changes how a whole set of words sounds.
The masculine article is normally il. But before s plus a consonant it becomes lo.
The trigger is s followed by another consonant — so it also covers
the psychologist, where the s is followed by p.
the sugar — z behaves the same way.
the standard. Borrowed words are not exempt: lo sport, lo staff.
In the plural every one of them takes gli.

sec-riflessivi.text: Reflexive verbs again, and now in the middle of ordinary sentences.
I sit at the desk. Two things there: sedersi is reflexive, and alla is a plus la.
Mi preparo per la lezione di italiano.
I get ready for the Italian lesson. Mi preparo has no tidy English equivalent — it is closer to I organise myself.
Are you getting your hair cut?
Quando sei a Napoli ti siedi al bar o sei in piedi?
When you're in Naples do you sit at the bar or stand? In piedi means standing.
We sit on the sofa — su plus il gives sul.

sec-incontrarsi.text: Some reflexives are reciprocal: the -si means each other.
Mi incontro con amici a Napoli.
I meet up with friends in Naples — and it keeps con.
Noi ci incontriamo in centro a Napoli.
We meet in the centre of Naples. In centro takes no article.
to deal with, to look after. It takes di, always.
Lei si occupa di appartamenti per i militari.
She handles apartments for the military.
We'll speak tomorrow — use that one when the next contact is by phone.

sec-ricordare.text: Remembering splits into two verbs in Italian.
I don't remember the name. Ricordare takes a direct object.
I don't remember. Ricordarsi is the reflexive, and more colloquial. Both are correct.
I don't remember anything. Italian requires the double negative — non and niente together.
The one that catches people: before a VERB you need di.
Non ricordo di prendere le medicine.
I don't remember to take the medicine.
Follow me. Notice the pronoun is attached on the end — an imperative does that, where the present tense puts it in front.

sec-contesto.text: Vocabulary from your own life, and the verb pair underneath it.
I know this place. Conoscere is for places and people.
I know how to speak Italian. Sapere is for facts and abilities. English uses know for both; Italian will not.
Lei si occupa di appartamenti per i militari.
She handles apartments for the military.
products with a lot of sugar.
Alla stessa ora, alle nove e cinquantacinque.
Same time, nine fifty-five. Unchanged since the first lesson.
